root_cause.text: In `drm/amdgpu/amdgpu_userq_vm_validate()`, the error path after `amdgpu_ttm_tt_get_user_pages()` could call `drm_exec_fini(&exec)` twice on the same `drm_exec` object because `new_addition` had already finalized `exec` before the loop, but failures still jumped to `unlock_all` where `drm_exec_fini()` was called again.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `if (ret) goto unlock_all;` to `if (ret) goto free_ranges;` specifically because “when new_addition is true, amdgpu_userq_vm_validate() calls drm_exec_fini(&exec) before iterating… If amdgpu_ttm_tt_get_user_pages() fails in that path, the code jumps to unlock_all and calls drm_exec_fini(&exec) a second time on the same exec object,” and the diff adds a separate `free_ranges:` label so the finalized `exec` is not finalized again.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the userqueue VM validation failure path to jump to the correct cleanup label when get_user_pages fails.
intent_record.what: In amdgpu_userq_vm_validate(), the error path for a failing amdgpu_ttm_tt_get_user_pages(bo, range) call was changed from `goto unlock_all;` to `goto free_ranges;`.
intent_record.how: On failure to pin user pages, execution now jumps to the cleanup path that frees the allocated range structures instead of only unlocking, which ensures the validation path performs the more appropriate cleanup for this error case.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a cleanup path to free XArray ranges after finalizing the DRM exec state.
intent_record.what: A new label, `free_ranges:`, was inserted immediately before the `xa_for_each(&xa, tmp_key, range)` loop in `amdgpu_userq_vm_validate()`. No other code in the hunk was changed.
intent_record.how: This creates an additional control-flow target so execution can jump directly to the range cleanup loop after `drm_exec_fini(&exec)`, allowing allocated or tracked ranges in the XArray to be released from this point.

It does not address the specific double-destruction bug in amdgpu_userq_vm_validate() where drm_exec_fini() could be called twice after amdgpu_ttm_tt_get_user_pages() failure.

candidates.rationale: On failure from amdgpu_ttm_tt_get_user_pages(), this jump sent execution to unlock_all, where drm_exec_fini(&exec) was performed again even though exec had already been finalized earlier by new_addition, causing a double fini on the same drm_exec object.

vuln_statements.explanation: This failure-path jump routes execution to unlock_all after amdgpu_ttm_tt_get_user_pages() fails, but exec had already been finalized by new_addition, so reaching unlock_all caused drm_exec_fini(&exec) to run a second time on the same object.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet clearly shows the vulnerable control flow. Inside `if (new_addition)`, the code explicitly calls `drm_exec_fini(&exec);` before retrying: `drm_exec_fini(&exec); ... invalidated = true; new_addition = false; goto retry_lock;`. However, later on the shared error path still unconditionally does `unlock_all: drm_exec_fini(&exec);`. This means if `amdgpu_ttm_tt_get_user_pages(bo, range)` fails in the `xa_for_each(&xa, tmp_key, range)` loop, execution jumps to `unlock_all` after `exec` has already been finalized, creating the double-finalization bug described in the root cause. The function does not contain any guard to prevent the second `drm_exec_fini()` call, so the fix is not present here.
